content.overview: Differences among results can arise from real lot heterogeneity, sampling, preparation, method and laboratory effects. Investigation should preserve all valid data and follow predefined retest authority.

vocabulary.definition: Parameter describing dispersion reasonably attributable to a measured value.
Result or trend that is unexpected and requires controlled evaluation without automatic invalidation.
Repeated testing or selective reporting intended to obtain a preferred outcome without justified investigation.

sections.title: Results have multiple variability sources
sections.body: Lot heterogeneity and analytical processes both contribute. Precision in the report does not eliminate upstream sampling uncertainty.

sections.title: Investigate before invalidating
sections.body: Original data, sample condition, method performance and laboratory communication should be preserved. A surprising result is not automatically wrong.

sections.title: Retesting follows controlled rules
sections.body: Retest, resample and report-amendment decisions need predefined authority and rationale. New results supplement rather than silently replace valid original results.

workedExamples: A resample differs from the first result; the investigation reviews lot heterogeneity and both sample histories rather than selecting the preferred value.
commonMistakes: Retesting until a passing result appears.
Discarding the original report after an amendment.
content.practicalApplication: Create an atypical-result review that separates lot, sampling, transport, laboratory and reporting hypotheses and records authorized next steps.
content.summary: Responsible result interpretation preserves all evidence and investigates variability under controlled retest rules.
